expected_survivors.name: the persisted state is reported as quarantined regardless
expected_survivors.why: A mutant in a REDUNDANT REPORTING PATH, not an equivalent mutant. It is identical only GIVEN that b11c persists before raising; were b11c to regress and raise without persisting, the hardcoded constant would hide exactly the regression the Q05 rehearsal exists to detect. The property is asserted independently by PrimaryEvidenceTests.test_the_state_file_on_disk_says_quarantined_after_exhausted_retries, which reads the file b11c actually wrote rather than this module's report. If that test is ever weakened this mutant stops being covered, which is why it is declared here instead of deleted.

expected_survivors.name: a terminal fault's retry count is faked
expected_survivors.why: Same shape. Identical only given that a non-retryable failure quarantines on the first call. Covered independently by PrimaryEvidenceTests.test_a_terminal_failure_really_calls_the_transport_once, which asserts the transport call count directly.

expected_survivors_note: Two. Both are mutants in a redundant reporting path whose underlying property is asserted independently elsewhere. 'Equivalent mutant' is the label that ends auditing; 'covered elsewhere' is the label that tells the next reader to check the coverage still exists. The codex seat corrected this wording in handoff 201 and the distinction is the reason these are declared rather than removed: if either starts being KILLED, the coverage that justifies it moved and the sweep will say so.
